quickAnswer: Chicagoland has the **only community-college NDT program in Illinois**: **Moraine Valley Community College** in Palos Hills, which says students can train in as little as **six weeks** [1][2]. Courses cover PT I & II, MT I & II, radiation safety, UT I and II and industrial radiography principles [4], with method courses costing around **$950–1,100** each [5][7]. The program is WIOA-approved, and the college notes formal on-the-job training with an employer is still required for certification [3]. Illinois requires industrial radiographers to hold **state certification** [10].

sections.h2: NDT training in Chicago: one standout program
paragraphs: Chicago has a huge industrial base — steel and metals, manufacturing, refining, rail, aerospace components and utilities — and therefore steady NDT demand. For training, one name dominates: Moraine Valley Community College in the south-west suburbs. Moraine Valley describes its program as the only community-college NDT program in Illinois [2] and says it offers an entire basic-level NDT program that can be completed in as little as six weeks [1].
For Chicagoans, that means an affordable, local, structured route into the field without relocating — a real advantage compared with many US cities.

sections.h2: Inside the Moraine Valley NDT program
paragraphs: Moraine Valley's NDT classes include liquid penetrant (PT I & II), magnetic particle (MT I & II), radiation safety, longitudinal ultrasonic evaluation (UT I), ultrasonic testing Level 2 and industrial radiography principles (RT I) [4]. Its instructors emphasise teaching the basic disciplines most commonly used in NDT so students are familiar with all of them and have a better chance of finding work [1].

The college's catalogs give a sense of cost and intensity. A recent spring catalog lists Magnetic Particle (MT I & II) at $950 [5], an earlier catalog lists Industrial Radiography Principles (RT I) at $1,100 [5][7], and one NDT course is described as 75 hours of classroom instruction and 150 hours of hands-on training [7]. The college has invested in current equipment, including a multi-directional magnetic particle inspection system [8], and it has recruited Level 3 instructors to teach topics including ultrasonic testing, radiography, radiation safety, eddy current and phased arrays [9].
Classes run in day, night and open-entry formats, and the program is approved for WIOA funding through the local workforce area [3].

sections.h2: From Moraine Valley certificate to industry certification
paragraphs: Moraine Valley is clear that its certificate of completion is not the same as industry certification: formal on-the-job training is required for certification by a qualified employer who offers formal testing, and graduates can go on to earn credentials from ASNT [3]. That matches how SNT-TC-1A works nationwide — the school supplies classroom and lab hours, and the employer's written practice, Level III and supervised experience complete the certification.
For most graduates, the next step is a trainee role with an inspection company, fabricator, steel producer or refinery contractor, followed by Level II certification in the methods the employer uses.

Moraine Valley runs a free online informational session about NDT careers, pitched as a way to learn about a trade that pays well right out of high school, and offers a $350 Intro to Nondestructive Testing course [6]. Its catalog describes NDT professionals as the safety experts behind the scenes, inspecting everything from aircraft parts to oil pipelines and roller coasters [5].
Taking the introduction first is a low-risk way to confirm the work suits you before paying for multiple method courses.

sections.h2: Funding and scheduling for working adults
paragraphs: One reason Moraine Valley suits Chicago residents is flexibility. The program offers day classes, night classes and open-entry/exit options, and it is approved for Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) funding through the local workforce area, with books and fees listed at about $600 of the total program cost [3]. Residents who qualify for WIOA support may be able to cover much of the program cost.

The college also has campuses in Blue Island and Tinley Park in addition to Palos Hills [5], which helps students across the south and south-west suburbs. Working adults often take one method at a time in the evenings while keeping their current job, then switch to NDT once they have enough methods to be hired as a trainee.

sections.h2: Steel, refining and heavy industry around Chicago
paragraphs: Chicago's position as a steel, metals and heavy-manufacturing centre gives NDT trainees a wide choice of employers. Steel producers and processors inspect plate, bar and pipe with ultrasonic and electromagnetic methods; fabricators use magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic testing on structural and pressure welds; and refineries and chemical plants in the south suburbs and north-west Indiana run large turnaround programs that need radiography, ultrasonic thickness testing and visual inspection.

Turnaround seasons in particular create short bursts of high demand, which can be a good way for newly trained technicians to gain experience quickly with contractors that supply crews to these plants.

sections.h2: Where Chicago NDT jobs come from
paragraphs: Chicagoland's NDT work spans steel mills and metals processors, heavy fabrication and manufacturing, refineries and chemical plants in the south suburbs and north-west Indiana, rail equipment and infrastructure, aerospace component suppliers and power utilities. Magnetic particle and penetrant testing are everyday methods in fabrication and manufacturing; ultrasonic testing is used for welds, thickness and castings; and radiography supports pressure equipment and pipeline work.
Trainees who complete Moraine Valley's full set of courses arrive with exposure to all of these methods, which helps them fit into whatever crew an employer needs to staff.

Illinois runs its own radiographer certification. Under 32 Ill. Adm. Code 405, individuals must meet the state's requirements for certification to work as industrial radiographers [10]. The state's industrial radiography rules in 32 Ill. Adm. Code 350 set training and testing requirements [11] and require radiographers to carry their certification cards at the job site [12].

That is why Moraine Valley includes a radiation safety course alongside radiography principles [4]: trainees who want to work as radiographers need both the radiation-safety training and the supervised experience required before state certification.

sections.h2: How NDT certification actually works for Chicago trainees
paragraphs: The most common misunderstanding about NDT training is that a school certifies you. In the United States, the documents most employers follow are ASNT's Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A, the ANSI/ASNT CP-189 standard and the CP-105 topical outlines [20]. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification is employer-based: a school or online course supplies the classroom hours, but your employer's written practice, its Level III and your documented on-the-job experience are what turn training into a certification. Training programs therefore combine formal classroom or online theory with on-the-job training (OJT) performed in a field or lab setting [20].

In practice, a new technician in any city follows the same ladder: complete Level I and then Level II classroom hours for a method, log supervised experience, pass the employer's general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and receive Level II certification in that method. Level III — the person who writes procedures, approves techniques and certifies others — requires additional experience and, for most employers, the ASNT NDT Level III examinations.

sections.h2: Training hours you will need by method
paragraphs: SNT-TC-1A publishes recommended minimum classroom hours by method and level for high-school-educated candidates [13]. Employers can adopt stricter numbers in their written practice, and aerospace employers working to NAS 410 or customers with their own specifications often do. Visual testing shows the scale of supervised experience involved: SNT-TC-1A recommends 8 training hours for VT Level I and 16 more for Level II, with 70 and 140 hours of experience in the method respectively [14].

sections.h2: Industrial radiography: the extra licensing layer in Chicago
paragraphs: Radiography is the one method where federal and state radiation-safety law sits on top of SNT-TC-1A. Under 10 CFR 34.43, a licensee may not let anyone act as a radiographer until the person has received training in the required radiation-safety subjects, completed at least two months of on-the-job training and been certified through a radiographer certification program by a certifying entity [15][16]. ASNT's Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) program is one such certifying entity; it combines a computer-based exam with an employer-conducted practical exam and vision check, and many states recognize it [17]. Online radiation-safety courses such as AWS's roughly 40-hour eLearning module can supply the classroom portion, but site-specific training from the employer is still required [18].
In Illinois, state certification under 32 Ill. Adm. Code 405 and the job-site card requirement in Part 350 apply on top of these federal concepts [10][12].

Published industry guidance puts classroom training for a single method at roughly USD 600–2,000, with examination fees of roughly USD 200–500 on top [19]. ASNT lists the initial IRRSP combination exam for radioactive-material and X-ray radiography at USD 260 for members and USD 285 for non-members [17]. Longer certificate and associate-degree programs cost more but bundle several methods, labs and job placement support, and community-college options are often eligible for financial aid.

Before paying, ask whether the price includes the practical hours, specimens and exam fees, whether the course is written to SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or NAS 410, and whether the provider will document your hours in a form an employer's Level III can accept.

sections.h2: How to choose an NDT training provider
paragraphs: Use this checklist to compare schools, online courses and employer programs.
bullets: Training hours that meet or exceed the SNT-TC-1A table for each method and level.
Hands-on labs with real-flaw specimens, not just slides and videos.
Instructors who hold ASNT Level III in the method they teach.
Documentation of hours suitable for an employer's written practice.
A path to OJT — employer partnerships, apprenticeships or placement support.
For radiography, preparation for IRRSP or the state radiographer exam.
Transparent total cost including exams, books and specimens.

paragraphs: NDT's workforce is ageing: the PQNDT salary and benefits survey put the average NDT technician's age at 47 [21]. As experienced technicians retire, employers across energy, aerospace, infrastructure and manufacturing need trained replacements, which is why so many now sponsor training, apprenticeships and on-the-job programs for motivated newcomers.
A practical sequence for Chicago beginners:
bullets: Attend Moraine Valley's free NDT info session [6].
Take PT and MT, then UT and radiation safety [4].
Ask about WIOA funding through your local workforce office [3].
Get hired as a trainee to complete on-the-job training for certification [3].
If you want radiography, plan for Illinois state certification [10].
Join the local ASNT section to meet Level IIIs and employers who hire Moraine Valley graduates.
Look for turnaround contractors serving south-suburban and north-west Indiana refineries to build hours quickly.
Keep copies of every course certificate and log your on-the-job hours from day one.

faqs.q: Where can I get NDT training in Chicago?
faqs.a: Moraine Valley Community College in Palos Hills runs the only community-college NDT program in Illinois [2].

faqs.q: How long does Moraine Valley's NDT program take?
faqs.a: The college says students can complete training in as little as six weeks [1], although many working adults spread courses over a semester or longer.

faqs.q: How much do Moraine Valley NDT courses cost?
faqs.a: Recent catalogs list MT I & II at $950 and RT I at $1,100 [5][7].

faqs.q: Does Moraine Valley certify NDT technicians?
faqs.a: It awards a certificate of completion; formal on-the-job training with a qualified employer is required for industry certification [3].

faqs.q: Do radiographers need state certification in Illinois?
faqs.a: Yes, under 32 Ill. Adm. Code 405, and they must carry their cards at job sites [10][12].

faqs.q: Can I get funding for NDT training in Chicago?
faqs.a: Moraine Valley's NDT program is WIOA approved [3], so eligible residents should ask their local workforce office about funding before enrolling.
